provenance_note: Expected values recorded from an independently authored corpus written from SPEC-repairreplace.md without the page code; this run executes the shipping build against them and re-derives nothing.
reference: The model is the deterministic expected-value life-cycle cost of IEC 60300-3-3: each option's costs (investment and outage at implementation and at like-for-like renewals, yearly opex, expected failures times the cost of one failure including its downtime, expected risk cost) are discounted at the real rate r, investments at their exact time and recurring costs at the end of each year, with a straight-line residual value credited at the horizon; options are ranked by present value and compared through the equivalent annual cost. Expected failure counts come from a homogeneous rate, a power-law NHPP (minimal repair; Crow-AMSAA estimates for time-terminated data, Rigdon & Basu 2000) or a Weibull renewal process (as good as new; renewal function solved by a Stieltjes-trapezoid scheme of the Xie 1989 type on the grid the specification prescribes; Weibull parameters by censored maximum likelihood, Lawless 2003).
reference_citations: IEC 60300-3-3:2017 Dependability management - Part 3-3: Application guide - Life cycle costing. https://webstore.iec.ch/publication/27720
Crow, L.H. (1974) Reliability analysis for complex, repairable systems. In: Proschan, F., Serfling, R.J. (eds.) Reliability and Biometry, SIAM, Philadelphia, pp. 379-410.
Rigdon, S.E., Basu, A.P. (2000) Statistical Methods for the Reliability of Repairable Systems. Wiley, New York.
Lawless, J.F. (2003) Statistical Models and Methods for Lifetime Data, 2nd ed. Wiley, Hoboken (Weibull maximum likelihood with right censoring).
Xie, M. (1989) On the solution of renewal-type integral equations. Communications in Statistics - Simulation and Computation 18(1):281-293.
tolerance: All tolerances are relative. Default 1e-9 for PV, EAC, components and year-table values of cases using rate, nhpp or none models: these are closed-form sums, and the reference was matched to 1e-9 by an independent route. Cases with Weibull renewal counts carry tol 1e-4 (pv, eac, years, renewal); the reference values are the 2 000-step values of the rev .2 §4 scheme (Xie 1989), and each was checked against a 16x finer grid of the same scheme (agreement better than 2e-5). Renewal-dependent values are graded only inside the rev .2 domain beta >= 1, t_max/eta <= 60; the graded Weibull cases have beta 1-3.5 and t_max/eta <= 3. The beta = 1 case keeps the exact rate values (M = t/eta), which the scheme reproduces to 1e-7. Fitted parameters 1e-9 (bisection to 1e-12 relative). Thresholds 1e-6 as the specification allows; the reference threshold is the boundary of the preferred option including a change to a tie, i.e. where PV(challenger) - PV(preferred) = max(0.005 EUR, 1e-9 x largest |PV|); this boundary differs from the exact PV crossing by up to 1.4e-6 relative in case thresholds_rate_models, which therefore carries tol 2e-6 so that both readings pass. Integers, booleans, indices, lists of gap ids and refusal reasons are graded exactly. 'gaps' lists the complete set expected (order-free); 'no_gaps' lists gap ids that must be absent. Partial component dictionaries grade only the keys given.
not_benchmarked: decision_approved and the input fingerprint (§9): not graded by the corpus per rev .2 §11 (internal hash).
Warnings text (scenario basis after a refused fit, never-implemented option): content and wording are not specified; only the resulting numbers and fit_refused codes are graded.

The margin PV(second) - PV(first) and the name of a lowest-cost inadmissible option: §6 defines them but §10 gives no expect key; the lowest_cost_inadmissible case grades pv, ranking and preferred instead.
The PVs of every sensitivity, band and threshold run: only the boolean sensitivity_changes, band preferred options/holds and threshold boundaries are graded.
Weibull renewal counts for beta < 1 (outside the graded domain of rev .2 §4): case weibull_beta07_new grades only the ranking.
Thresholds and sensitivity for studies with Weibull models, and studies where a threshold coincides with a renewal leaving the horizon (PV discontinuity).

Whether option_incomplete is also raised as a gap when the existing model is unresolved (rev .2 §8 says no option is then complete, but the option_incomplete row does not list that cause): cases with an unresolved existing model expect gaps = [existing_failure] only, following the literal gap table.
Non-integer horizon, report, PDF, state codec, presets UI and the seven languages.

manifest.note: Manifest v2 accepted by catalog.php under engineering-change; zero errors; since 1.2 the manifest carries entry, medium and lifecycle only, and every edge lives in workflow-map.json.

localisation.note: Opened in en, uk, de, nl, fr, es and pl: <html lang> follows the site language, no undefined/NaN/[object Object] rendered, no console errors; the default study is built in the reader's language.

mobile_desktop.note: Rendered at 390, 768, 769 and 1440 px with no root horizontal overflow; the result strip carries the preferred option, its present value and the margin.

permalink_round_trip.note: Each of the six examples opened from its permalink in a fresh page reproduces the state and every record output exactly.

presets.note: Six editable examples (pump, control at 0 %, drive with a fitted Weibull history, air-handling unit upgrade, problem with a refused fit and a scenario band, plant LTO scope), applied in en and uk with complete records.

learn_mode.note: Eight topics and a seven-step tour, including the try / explanation / correction case on the lead-time threshold.

report_all_languages.note: Report built in all seven languages, four A4 pages with the source line on every page, the chart supplied as a figure, no repeated sentence over 45 characters, no English sentence left in the other six.

python_export.note: The exported script runs on a bare python3 and its self-test reproduces 19 values (PV, EAC, components, ranking, preferred, tie) within 1e-9 relative; a 40-state random parity of the ported core agrees to 1.6e-15.

benchmark_regeneration_parity.note: window.__dgcBenchmark() regenerates the shipped artifact; reference_sha256 equals the deployed corpus.

console.note: No uncaught page errors in the language, layout, example, round-trip, report and python runs.

cases.note: Failure ages 0 and −1 are ignored before the fit: Crow-AMSAA on n = 3 (2.5, 5, 8), T = 9: β̂ = 3 / Σ ln(9/tᵢ), η̂ = 9 / 3^(1/β̂). [§4]
Weibull history 0, 4, 7: the 0 is ignored, two failures remain — too_few_failures; the scenario rate 0.15 is used. [§4]
NHPP not repairable and only 2 failures: the repairable check runs first; the scenario rate 0.6 is used. [§4]
NHPP with unknown end and only 2 failures: observation_end is checked before too_few_failures; the scenario rate 0.6 is used. [§4]
NHPP with every failure at the end of observation: Σ ln(T/tᵢ) = 0 — degenerate; the scenario rate 0.6 is used. [§4]
Weibull with two equal failures: too_few_failures is checked before degenerate; the scenario rate 0.15 is used. [§4]
An option never implemented (lead 120 = 12·H) still carries its risks every year: PV = PV(continue) + 1000 × a(5 %, 10); continue preferred. [§5]
life = 0: no renewal and no residual value; replace PV = 6000 + 1000 + 10 × 500 = 12 000 at r = 0. [§5]
NHPP fit refused (2 failures); the scenario rate 0.8 with low 0.2 / high 1.2 takes part in the band: same numbers as band_breaks — continue at the low end, replace at base and high end. [§4, §7.2]

Pump with downtime cost 0: the downtime parameter stays 0 at both ends — no change in its row. [§7.1]
Existing Weibull fit refused without a scenario rate: the existing model is unresolved, no option is complete — not even a replacement at t = 0 — so no PV at all; calculation not completed. [§8, §9]
B and C within 0.005 EUR, C cheaper: ranking [2, 1, 0]; tied listed in ranking order [2, 1]. [§6]
